skill.name: homeassistant-config
skill.description: Create and review Home Assistant YAML for automations, scripts, templates, blueprints, Lovelace dashboards, and configuration organization.
skill.summary: Build Home Assistant YAML, dashboards, blueprints, and validation workflows with local examples and checks.
skill.author: ESJavadex

security_audit.summary: AI review found the static findings to be false positives from Home Assistant examples, Markdown syntax, and local validation scripts. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, unauthorized network access, or malicious command execution was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Example secrets and camera URLs use realistic placeholder shapes.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly fake values and documentation-reserved addresses to reduce future scanner noise.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger shell-execution heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Label all commands as user-run local validators and state that the skill does not execute them automatically.

remediation.issue: The hidden .storage Lovelace example can look like broad hidden-file access.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that users should pass only their own Home Assistant Lovelace storage file when validating dashboards.

content.value_statement: Home Assistant YAML is easy to break when automations, secrets, and dashboards grow. This skill provides patterns, examples, and local validators for safer configuration work.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Home Assistant automation, script, scene, template, and blueprint YAML.
Explains 2024+ Home Assistant syntax for triggers, actions, and conditions.
Provides Lovelace dashboard and custom card examples.
Runs local validators for YAML syntax, Lovelace cards, and duplicate automations.
Suggests file organization patterns and secrets management practices.
Troubleshoots common entity, service, template, and indentation errors.
limitations: It does not connect to a running Home Assistant server.
Generated YAML must be reviewed with your real entity IDs.
Local validators require Python and PyYAML installed in the environment.
It cannot confirm third-party custom cards are installed in your instance.

use_cases.title: Create Reliable Automations
use_cases.description: Generate motion lighting, presence, climate, and notification automations using current YAML structure.

use_cases.title: Validate Configuration Changes
use_cases.description: Check YAML files, dashboard cards, duplicate rules, and common Home Assistant mistakes before reloading.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Configurations
use_cases.description: Use examples and best practices to organize files, secrets, dashboards, and reusable blueprints.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Home Assistant automation for this goal: [goal]. Use these entities: [entities]. Explain what I should replace.

prompt_templates.title: Fix YAML Validation Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Home Assistant YAML error and file excerpt. Identify the likely cause and provide a corrected version.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Lovelace View
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Lovelace dashboard view for [room or workflow]. Include cards for these entities: [entity list].

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Automations Into Blueprints
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related Home Assistant automations. Propose a reusable blueprint, required inputs, and migration steps.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a motion light automation with a five minute timeout.
output: A concise automation plan with trigger, condition, and action sections.
A note to replace sample entity IDs with real Home Assistant entities.
Validation reminders for indentation, quoted states, and automation mode.

output_examples.input: A user shares a Lovelace card that fails to load.
output: A diagnosis of missing card type, invalid entity reference, or action syntax.
A corrected dashboard structure described in plain language.
A follow-up checklist for HACS custom cards and Developer Tools checks.

output_examples.input: A user wants to clean a large Home Assistant configuration directory.
output: A file organization plan for automations, scripts, sensors, and secrets.
Suggestions for duplicate detection and local validation commands.
Guidance to keep secrets and database files out of version control.

best_practices: Validate YAML locally before restarting or reloading Home Assistant.
Keep real passwords, tokens, coordinates, and database files out of version control.
Test templates, entity IDs, and services in Home Assistant Developer Tools first.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real secrets into prompts, examples, repositories, or shared logs.
Do not apply generated automations without checking entity names and service support.
Do not mix old and new Home Assistant automation syntax in the same rule.

faq.question: Can this skill edit my live Home Assistant instance?
faq.answer: No. It works with local files and examples. You decide when to apply changes to Home Assistant.

faq.question: Does it support the newer Home Assistant automation syntax?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance favors current trigger, condition, and action structure used by recent Home Assistant releases.

faq.question: Can it validate Lovelace dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a local validator for YAML dashboards and Home Assistant storage-style Lovelace data.

faq.question: Will it protect my secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains secrets practices, but you must avoid sharing real passwords, tokens, and coordinates.

faq.question: Can it find duplicate automations?
faq.answer: Yes. The included duplicate finder compares automations and scripts for exact matches, similar rules, and trigger conflicts.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No. The included scripts operate on local files. Some examples mention Home Assistant documentation links.
